# PLAN — iteration 2

## Current state assessment
Iteration 1’s balanced, registered partial sums improved setup WNS from −9.918 ns to −2.95 ns while hold remained positive at 0.121 ns, but timing is still infeasible at the 6.667 ns clock period. The current seed preserves the known one-cycle annotation and uses two 32-bit partial-sum registers; the prior doctor trial was not adopted because simulation was unverified, so it provides no evidence of candidate performance.

## Hypothesis
For the default symmetric coefficients, pairing the corresponding delayed samples before multiplication may reduce DSP and accumulation logic enough to improve setup timing, while an elaboration-time fallback preserves behavior for nonsymmetric parameter values.

## Instruction for generator
Keep the existing `d[0:7]` delay line and pipeline registers, and add a parameter-conditional symmetric-coefficient path that pairs `d[0]+d[7]`, `d[1]+d[6]`, `d[2]+d[5]`, and `d[3]+d[4]` before multiplying by their common coefficients. Preserve the full 17-bit signed pair sums and 32-bit modulo result semantics, then feed balanced pair products into the existing registered partial sums. Retain the general per-tap product path whenever any coefficient pair differs; preserve synchronous reset behavior, output cycles, and `// @latency 1`. The expected benefit is fewer multipliers and a shorter accumulation chain for the default coefficients; confirm the actual effect with the unchanged simulation and routed timing, hold, and utilization gates.
